note: Forward predictions for 1.18, authored by the pred-scout-coach agent on session compute (no API) and grounded in the 2026-11-02 baseline: pred.gg ranked lane stats for the patch 1.17 family (version ids 167+168+169, ~198,150 matches) and the 1.17.2 public match stream perk counts (augments and Eternals), plus 1.17.2 Eternal usage and finished-item samples. Forecasts, not measured results; no 1.18 games have been counted. Kaelen has no data at all and is absent from data/catalog until pred.gg publishes 1.18, so his entry is a kit-only read. The kit-math sim was not used.

kaelen.name: Kaelen
changes: NEW HERO, melee physical frontliner. 695 health (+131), 310 mana (+60), 65 physical power (+5.2), 135 attack speed (+2.2), 36 physical armor (+4.8), 31 magical armor (+1.7), 700 movement speed, BAT 1.5.
Heart of Ice (passive): abilities leave Rimeglass for 6s. Enemies on it get Frostbite for 1s: 15% slow and 0.5% max health true damage every 0.5s.
Pale Twins (basic): melee, 325u range, 25% cleave, 65 (+80% bonus physical power).

Razorstorm (primary): spins for 3.5s, hitting every 0.25s in 400u for 7.5-17.5 (+8-16% total physical power) (+0.5-1.8% max health), laying Rimeglass. Cannot be interrupted by hard crowd control. 60% against minions. Passively +4-12% armors, x1.5 on Rimeglass. 13-8s cooldown.

Winter's Pursuit (secondary): 1100u dash that stops past the first hero, 70-170 (+100% bonus physical power) and a 25% slow for 1.2s; against a Frostbitten target damage doubles and heroes are rooted for 1.2s instead. 16-14s cooldown.
Rimefang (alternate): 0.6s channel, then a spirit flies 2250u through terrain dealing 11-15% of the target's max health, a 0.2s stun and a 50% slow for 1.5s, trailing Rimeglass. 15-13s cooldown.

Frostfall (ultimate): 1.5s channel, then 4s in the sky at 1275 movement speed, over walls and immune to damage; lands for 200/300/400 (+100% bonus physical power) (+6% bonus health), a 40% slow, a 1.5s root in the center, and an 8s Frost Storm that keeps applying Frostbite at double damage. 130/110/90s cooldown.

Augments: Relentless Hunt (Razorstorm hits once more per 20% attack speed, up to +10, and can crit; Rimeglass no longer grants armor), Neverending Chase (hits on heroes and camp leaders cut Winter's Pursuit cooldown 3%), Last Winter (allies in the landing zone get +20% movement speed; Kaelen gets a 10% max health +4% per hero hit shield).
kaelen.why: Every ability lays Rimeglass, and enemies standing on it take Frostbite: a 15% slow and 0.5% max health true damage every 0.5s. Winter's Pursuit doubles its damage and roots for 1.2s against a Frostbitten target, and Frostfall gives him 4s in the sky, immune to damage, before a landing that roots the center for 1.5s.
kaelen.willChange: We hold no data on him at all, and he is absent from our catalog until pred.gg publishes 1.18, so this is a kit-only read, including the offlane role. The notes call him a frontliner and name Forticus for him, and Razorstorm keeps spinning through hard crowd control, which points at offlane first and jungle second. Expect him to show up in a lot of early drafts while players learn him. To play against him, stay off his Rimeglass, because Frostbite lingers for 1s after you leave it and Winter's Pursuit roots any target that is still Frostbitten.

valmont.name: Baron Valmont
changes: Hemophagia mana restore 3-38 -> 3-33
Rupture magical power scaling 15% -> 16%
Exsanguinate damage 40/65/90 -> 40/62/84, scaling 23% -> 20%; hero healing 20/40/60 -> 16/34/52, scaling 22% -> 20%
Exsanguinate minion healing modifier 10% -> 12.5%, minion healing 1.8/3.6/5.4 -> 2/4.25/6.5, scaling 2.2% -> 2.5%
Sanguine Banquet omnivamp bonus mana scaling 0.4% -> 0.35%
valmont.why: Exsanguinate's damage drops from 40/65/90 to 40/62/84 with scaling 23% -> 20%, and its hero healing from 20/40/60 to 16/34/52 with scaling 22% -> 20%. Rupture's magical scaling rises from 15% to 16% and his passive mana restore falls from 3-38 to 3-33.
valmont.willChange: He sat at 53.5% over 15,732 ranked midlane games across the 1.17 family, but that window includes the weeks before the 1.17.2 nerf; the 1.17.2 match stream had him at 51.3% over 5,338 midlane games. Expect another step down, mostly in long fights the ultimate used to win on its own. Open with Rupture and your basic attacks before pressing Exsanguinate instead of using the ultimate to walk in. Sanguine Banquet was his most-played augment by far at 4,727 games and 52.1%, and it loses a little more mana scaling, so check the site's augment card rather than assuming it stays the pick.

maco.name: Maco
changes: Health regen 1.6 -> 1.3; attack speed 115 -> 125; BAT 1.3 -> 1.45
Maco Gift! health magical power scaling 35% -> 40%; healing allies now grants Maco the assist
Maco Fly! shield 60/115/170/225/280 -> 60/110/160/210/260, magical power scaling 50% -> 60%
Maco Sparkle! stun 1.1-1.3s -> 1-1.2s, minimum stun 0.5s -> 0.35s
Shatterbloom healing magical power scaling 4% -> 4.5%; Ferocious Flight shield scaling 12% -> 15%, cooldown refund 1s -> 1.5s
maco.why: Maco Gift! healing scaling rises from 35% to 40% and Maco Fly!'s shield scaling from 50% to 60%, while its flat shield drops to 60/110/160/210/260. Maco Sparkle!'s stun shortens to 1-1.2s with a 0.35s minimum, and his base health regen falls from 1.6 to 1.3.
maco.willChange: He sat at 47.0% over 11,534 ranked support games, and the notes say he struggled most in the average match. The notes say the changes move his value away from tank builds and into magical power. Expect a modest climb for healing and shield builds, with the shorter stun making the close-range stun-into-ultimate play less reliable. Both main augments get scaling, Shatterbloom (48.2% over 2,127 games) and Ferocious Flight (44.7% over 2,087), so let the site's augment card choose between them.

skylar.name: Skylar
changes: Plasma Grenade slow 40-60% -> 45-65%
Air Assault missile scaling 20% bonus physical -> 16%, 12% magical -> 10%; cooldown 24/22/20/18/16 -> 21/19.75/18.5/17.25/16
Hypercharge bonus physical armor penetration 20% -> 25%; damage ramp per hit 1% -> 0.75%, max stacks 25 -> 30, max ramp 25% -> 22.5%
Plasma Barrage explosion missing health damage 6% -> 7.5%; Atomised Artillery time between shots 0.75s -> 0.65s and now +10 ultimate haste
skylar.why: Air Assault's missile scaling drops (20% -> 16% bonus physical, 12% -> 10% magical) while its cooldown starts at 21 instead of 24, and Hypercharge's damage ramp now tops out at 22.5% instead of 25% while its armor penetration rises from 20% to 25%. Plasma Grenade slows harder, and Plasma Barrage and Atomised Artillery both get stronger.
skylar.willChange: She sat at 48.2% over 24,091 ranked carry games, mostly on Assault MK-II (8,970 games, 48.6%). The fly-and-beam pattern loses damage while her grenade, armor penetration and augments gain, which the notes frame as a better answer to tanks. Expect a sideways move rather than a clear rise, and expect some players to try Plasma Barrage (47.9% over 2,181) or Atomised Artillery (46.2% over 961); follow the site's augment card once 1.18 games come in. Hexbound Bracers' bigger basic attack block is also aimed partly at her.

legion.name: Legion
changes: Saturation Charge cooldown 19/18/17/16/15 -> 18/17/16/15/14
Frag Order damage 70/110/150/190/230 -> 80/120/160/200/240; bonus physical scaling 60-80% -> 65-85%; magical scaling 40% -> 60%
Press The Advantage fire rate 12-28% -> 14-30%
Napalm Zone damage 5 -> 7, bonus physical scaling 6% -> 7%
Heavy Caliber damage modifier 310% -> 300%
Bugfix: K-75 Storm Rifle now executes minions at the correct threshold
legion.why: Saturation Charge's cooldown drops to 18/17/16/15/14 from 19/18/17/16/15, and Frag Order hits for 80/120/160/200/240 with magical scaling 40% -> 60%. Press The Advantage fires faster and Napalm Zone hits harder, while Heavy Caliber's damage modifier drops from 310% to 300%.
legion.willChange: He was already above average at 51.4% over 47,619 ranked carry games, so this pushes a strong, heavily played carry further up. Heavy Caliber was his best-performing augment at 52.8% over 2,714 games and the only one cut, while Press the Advantage, the most played at 10,346 games and 50.0%, is raised. Expect his early lane to feel safer and his win rate to drift up; the notes say they will watch him. If you are the frontliner into him, Hexbound Bracers now blocks 8 (+1 per level) per basic attack, up from 5 (+1 per level).

kira.name: Kira
changes: Nevermore (passive raven) damage (+7% target's current health) -> 15/30/45/60 by level 1/6/11/16 (+5% target's current health)
Dusk bonus physical power scaling per stack 12% -> 15%
kira.why: Her passive raven now deals 15/30/45/60 by level 1/6/11/16 plus 5% of the target's current health, instead of 7% current health alone, so it hits low-health targets and minions harder. Dusk's bonus physical scaling per stack rises from 12% to 15%.
kira.willChange: She sat at 49.1% over 27,660 ranked carry games and 47.2% over 1,477 in the high band. The flat raven damage helps her trade and clear in lane, but Solaris, finished in 1,489 of her builds at 52.2%, drops from 15 to 10 ability haste. Expect a small net gain: the raven helps her lane, and the Dusk scaling helps her longer fights later on. Keep Solaris while the site's build card still ranks it; the notes say it is meant for her and TwinBlast.

kallari.name: Kallari
changes: Crippling Dagger bonus physical power scaling 85% -> 90%, slow 25% -> 30%
Bugfix: double jump now goes on cooldown if she is interrupted out of it
kallari.why: Crippling Dagger's bonus physical scaling rises from 85% to 90% and its slow from 25% to 30%. Her double jump now goes on cooldown if she is interrupted out of it.
kallari.willChange: She sat at 46.6% over 12,346 ranked jungle games, though the high band had her at 52.6% over 652, so she may reward experience. A slightly stronger dagger helps poke and set up mid-range fights but does not change her all-in. Expect a small rise at most. Her Eternals split widely, with Lotus at 50.3% over 2,127 games and Vesh at 41.7% over 1,427, so follow the site's Eternal card.

serath.name: Serath
changes: Physical power growth 2.6 -> 3.3 per level
serath.why: Physical power growth rises from 2.6 to 3.3 per level, and Chastise hits for 80/110/140/170/200 instead of 80/105/130/155/180. Both gains grow with level, so the help lands in the mid game.
serath.willChange: She sat at 49.1% over 33,898 ranked jungle games, and the notes say she needed an early lead to matter. Expect more power per level to let her scale without one and her number to move toward even. Her Eternal split is wide, Weald at 50.8% over 8,065 games against Thraex at 45.9% over 4,935, so check the site's Eternal card before copying an old build. Offlane Serath, at 42.2% over 3,675 games, is still a jungler played out of seat.

iggy-scorch.name: Iggy & Scorch
changes: Flame Turret takes 2x damage from melee basic attacks, up from 1.7x
iggy-scorch.why: Flame Turret now takes 2x damage from melee basic attacks, up from 1.7x. Nothing else in the kit changes.
iggy-scorch.willChange: The target is his offlane, where he sat at 54.4% over 13,954 ranked games and usually faces melee laners; his main role, midlane, sat at 50.4% over 26,887 and mostly faces ranged mages the change does not touch. Expect the offlane number to come down while midlane stays about where it was. Melee offlaners into him should walk up and hit the turrets, which now fall faster; Iggy players should place turrets where reaching them costs tower or minion damage.

morigesh.name: Morigesh
changes: Movement speed 675 -> 670
Cursed Infestation hive damage +12% -> +10%
morigesh.why: Cursed Infestation's hive damage drops from +12% to +10% and her movement speed from 675 to 670. That slows her wave clear and poke a little and makes her easier to catch.
morigesh.willChange: Her midlane number, 48.2% over 22,182 ranked games, hides a strong high band at 53.9% over 1,285, and her offlane sat at 53.7% over 7,059. The notes aim at the offlane, where melee laners can now close the gap more easily. Expect a small dip in both seats. Cursed Infestation led her midlane augments at 50.2% over 5,694 games against Ritual Of Death at 47.0% over 4,773, so watch the site's augment card for that margin to narrow.

muriel.name: Muriel
changes: Alacrity shield 80/120/160/200/240 -> 80/115/150/185/220, magical power scaling 50% -> 60%
Reversal of Fortune damage reduction 30% -> 20% (+5% magical power)
muriel.why: Alacrity's flat shield drops to 80/115/150/185/220 while its magical scaling rises from 50% to 60%, and Reversal of Fortune's damage reduction changes from a flat 30% to 20% (+5% magical power).
muriel.willChange: She sat at 53.0% over 21,847 ranked support games and 53.9% over 1,984 in the high band, one of the strongest supports on the board. The cut lands on tank builds that skip magical power, which the notes say made her allies too hard to pick off. Expect her to stay strong with magical power and lose ground on full-tank builds. Buy a couple of magical power items before leaning on Alacrity and the ultimate; the notes say the shield only normalizes after that.

steel.name: Steel
changes: Physical armor 38 -> 35; health regen 2 -> 1.8
Bull Rush bonus health scaling 5% -> 6%
steel.why: His base physical armor drops from 38 to 35 and his health regen from 2 to 1.8, which makes level 1 easier to punish. Bull Rush's bonus health scaling rises from 5% to 6% to protect his offlane wave clear.
steel.willChange: He was one of the most played supports at 52.2% over 54,079 ranked games, while the high band had him at 47.3% over 1,737, and his offlane sat at 49.9% over 19,126. He is also hit through Krix, which he ran in 18,195 of 26,418 support games in the 1.17.2 stream at 52.4%. Expect duo-lane Steel to slip a little and offlane Steel to hold. Forticus and Vortex Stone are both named for him, so watch the site's build card as field data fills in rather than buying them on day one.

sectionMeta.tldr: 1.18 adds Kaelen, a frontliner with no data yet, plus two frontline items, Forticus and Vortex Stone, and trims the Eternals that handed out free gold, haste and health. Aion, Krix, Vesh and Demiurge lose value, while Knell and Xyris trade one minor's strength for another's. Timewarp's base mana regen also drops from 150% to 125%. Valmont is cut for a second straight patch, Maco, Kallari, Kira, Serath and Legion get help, and Steel's level-1 durability, Muriel's tank builds, Morigesh and Iggy's offlane come down. The ranked split also resets on release day, so expect the first week of lobbies to be noisy whatever the balance does.
sectionMeta.heroes: Twelve heroes are listed, and the changes mostly follow the measured board. Muriel at 53.0% over 21,847 ranked support games and Valmont at 53.5% over 15,732 midlane games take the clearest cuts, while Maco at 47.0% over 11,534 support games and Kallari at 46.6% over 12,346 jungle games get help. Legion is the exception: he is buffed from 51.4% over 47,619 carry games, with only Heavy Caliber trimmed. Skylar's damage moves out of her beam and missiles into the rest of her kit, and Kaelen arrives with no data at all.
sectionMeta.eternals: Seven Eternals change, and most of the changes remove value the notes call free. Aion's Major falls from 6% to 5% gold from ability damage and Philosopher from 4 to 3.5, on an Eternal that ran in 39,397 ranked games in the 1.17.2 window. Krix's Major drops from 5% to 4% max health, aimed at jungle bruisers, where it ran in 15,513 games at 51.4%. Construct goes from 1 to 0.75 ability haste per level and Phylactery from 100% to 75% cooldown progression, while Resonant Repair, Cull the Weak and Marrow's The Maw get small lifts. Pick by fit and let the site's Eternal cards, which rank by field edge, settle the replacements.
sectionMeta.items: Forticus and Vortex Stone are new and have no field data yet, so treat them as experiments until the site's build cards fill in. Solaris drops from 15 to 10 ability haste; it showed up in 8,575 finished inventories, led by TwinBlast at 3,916, and the notes want it off Eden and Yurei. Timewarp's base mana regen falls from 150% to 125% after 11,599 finished copies, with Dekker the top holder at 2,295, and Magnify's omnivamp drops from 10% to 8% after 11,392. Hexbound Bracers' basic attack block rises to 8 (+1 per level), Penumbra gets cheaper with more penetration, and Rebirth's Mechanica cooldown goes from 270 to 300.
sectionMeta.systems: Overclocked is a separate limited-time mode with no mana costs, +400 ability haste and fast objectives, and none of its hero, item, crest or Eternal numbers apply to ranked. The ranked-relevant system work is bug fixing: several dashes, leaps and teleports now carry the right tags, so effects such as Weald's Wind-Rider, Nihil's Inescapable and Berserker Axe or Envy now trigger off them. Towers no longer instantly retarget the moment their current target dies, and attack-chain heroes such as Scarlett now execute red-bar minions reliably. Momentum items no longer fire on the attack that reaches 100 stacks.
sectionMeta.ranked: Split 5 ends on release day and everyone re-places: 5 matches, or 10 if you are new to ranked or returning. Master is a new tier between Diamond I and Paragon, reached through a promotion game, with no VP cap and +11 / -11 VP per game, and Paragon becomes a live Top 100 that refreshes every 24 hours for players at 200+ VP in Master. Both tiers decay: you start Master with 10 banked days, each match banks a day up to 14, and an empty bank costs 25 VP a day. Losing with an AFK teammate now costs 5% to 25% of a normal loss, so a normal -18 becomes -1 to -4. Expect early-split lobbies to be noisy and uneven while everyone re-places, so read the first week's results with care.

comps.summary: Expect ranked drafts to lean further toward real frontlines: Kaelen arrives alongside Forticus, a tank item for fighters who stay in the fight, and Vortex Stone, an item for engage supports, while the Eternals that let mages and bruisers coast on free gold, haste and health all shrink. None of this is measured yet. These are reads from the changes and the 1.17 baseline, and the site's field data replaces them as 1.18 games come in.

shifts.text: Vortex Stone refunds 20% of basic cooldowns and shields when you immobilize a hero, which suits the engage supports the notes name, Riktor (50.0% over 47,720 ranked support games) and Adele (49.7% over 18,293). Forticus gives fighters an 8% max health shield when they take hero damage and grows them while the fight lasts. Expect comps built on one hard engage plus a fighter who can stand in the middle to get more attractive, with Kaelen's ultimate root as a new engage option.

shifts.lead: Haste-and-gold mage comps lose their cushion
shifts.text: Aion's gold, Philosopher, Arcane Resonance, Construct, Memory Leak, Phylactery and Timewarp's mana regen all come down together, so mages who leaned on Eternals for haste and gold now have to buy more of it. Expect a farming mid paired with a Timewarp support such as Dekker, whose 2,295 finished Timewarps won 48.2%, to scale a little slower and recover less from a lost lane. Valmont's ultimate cut also means a midlane dive around him needs setup from the jungle rather than one button.

shifts.lead: Jungle bruisers re-open the Eternal question
shifts.text: Krix ran in 15,513 jungle games at 51.4% in the 1.17.2 window, with Rampage and Aurora among its top users, and both its health and Predator shrink. Expect strong bruiser junglers such as Aurora (53.7% over 27,142) and Rampage (50.9% over 16,507) to stay in the pool, with some moving to another Eternal; let each hero's Eternal card on the site make that call. Serath's power growth buff adds a bruiser jungler who scales without an early lead.

shifts.lead: Maco and Muriel lean into magical power
shifts.text: Maco gets more healing and shield scaling, and Muriel's tank build loses flat shielding and ultimate damage reduction, so both push supports toward magical power. Expect comps that protect one carry with healing and shields to gain a little, and full-tank Muriel to lose ground, while Muriel built with magical power should stay strong. Across all builds she sat at 53.0% over 21,847 ranked support games. Steel support, at 52.2% over 54,079 games, loses level-1 armor and some of Krix, so the stonewall duo lane gets easier to bully early.

Legion, already at 51.4% over 47,619 carry games, gets an earlier spike, Kira gets flat raven damage for lane, and Skylar trades beam damage for anti-tank tools, while Solaris loses haste for every carry who buys it. Expect lane-bully carries to like the weaker level-1 Steel. Into fast attackers like Legion, Skylar and Eden, the notes name Hexbound Bracers' bigger block as the frontline answer.

Everyone plays 5 placement matches, 10 if new or returning, so expect early lobbies to mix skill levels. Comfort picks and simple comps tend to hold up better than new-hero experiments until ratings settle, and Kaelen's first week combines both problems. At the top, Master's +11 / -11 VP and Paragon's Top 100 reward steady play more than a single hot streak.
